answer: The memory doesn't say how to reveal the raw source on a read-only page. It does say you can copy a page or selection as clean Markdown (Export), and a widget view's ⋯ menu has **Copy as Markdown**, which stays available in read-only mode because only Bake is hidden there.
block:
--- API/widget.md ---
What a plain `${...}` renders | Widget menu and commands
Views docked above or below the page have the same ⋯ menu in their title bar (on hover, for a minimal frame), with **Go to definition** and **Copy as Markdown** where they apply. In a sidebar, the bottom panel or the modal, a content view’s header has it for **Copy as Markdown**. The dock menu and × stay beside it.

HTML-only widgets have no Markdown, so they have neither Copy nor Bake. Bake is hidden in read-only mode. *Baked Sections: Update* re-bakes fragments the same way.

Inline results have no button. Put the cursor in the `${...}` and run a command instead: *Widget: Copy*, *Widget: Bake*, or *Widget: Reload*. *Widgets: Refresh All* still re-runs every widget on the page.

--- Export.md ---
Support | description
Copy a page or selection as rich text or clean Markdown.

--- Guide/My First Markdown Page.md ---
Creating a page | [[Live Preview]] in action
As you’ll notice as you type, the markdown codes disappear when you move out your cursor, and the text renders as intended.

![Photo Walk with formatted headings, three task checkboxes and a Woodland Hike link.](../Screenshots/markdown-basics-preview.png)

A blank line separates paragraphs. `# Plan` becomes a heading, `*` starts a bullet, and `* [ ]` becomes an unchecked task. `[x]` is a completed task. `[[Woodland Hike]]` is a link to a page named `Woodland Hike`. The destination does not have to exist yet: follow the link and write content there whenever you’re ready to create it.

--- Guide/Reading These Docs.md ---
Read a page and reveal its source | Try a copied example
In your own pace, press **Cmd-k** on macOS or **Ctrl-k** on Windows/Linux, type `Markdown Practice`, and press **Shift-Enter**. Paste the block above into the page body. Move your cursor away to see a heading and an unchecked task. Click the checkbox to mark it complete. Your practice page changes, while this documentation stays unchanged.

--- CHANGELOG.md ---
CHANGELOG | Edge
* New `markdown.link(target, alias?)` makes a wiki link to a page or any object (by its `ref`), and nothing when there's nothing to link to. The query builder, docs and standard library use it instead of `"[[" .. p.name .. "]]"`. See [[API/markdown]].
  * `markdown.expandMarkdown` takes a `pageName` option to evaluate the text as that page instead of the open one. See [[API/markdown]].
  * **Potentially breaking:** `command.define`, `slashCommand.define`, `identity.define`, `taskState.define`, `codeWidget.define`, `virtualPage.define` and `syntax.define` now _merge_ repeated definitions with the same name, like `tag.define` already did, so you can e.g. define a tag’s schema in one place and add a `transform` elsewhere. Previously, each call replaced the whole definition.
